findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the portal server to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts against the instance.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised instance to exfiltrate data or reach command-and-control infrastructure without restriction.

findings.issue_category: hardcoded cloud credentials in user data
findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. EC2 user data is readable by anyone with instance metadata access (including via SSRF from the public web server), leaking long-lived credentials instead of using an IAM instance profile.
The instance declares no root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption settings, so the root volume may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.
No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains available and an SSRF flaw in the internet-facing Apache server could be used to read instance metadata and credentials.

The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and routed to an internet gateway with a wide-open security group, giving it a directly reachable public IP and maximizing attack surface.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (and no KMS key), so data stored on the attached disk is unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the resulting snapshot data is also unencrypted and could expose volume contents if shared or copied.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy restrictions are defined for the flow-log bucket, risking public or cross-account exposure of network traffic logs.

findings.issue_category: missing versioning and log integrity controls
findings.description: The bucket has force_destroy = true and no versioning or object lock, so audit-relevant flow logs can be silently deleted or overwritten by an attacker or an errant terraform destroy.
No server access logging is configured for the bucket holding VPC flow logs, so unauthorized access to the log archive would leave no trail.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, automatically exposing workloads to the internet.

A 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway is attached to the route table associated with both subnets, making every subnet public and removing any private-tier isolation.

No aws_default_security_group resource restricts the VPC's default security group, so it retains its permissive intra-group allow-all rules for any resource inadvertently launched without an explicit group.
